title: Extending norm and separated minimal-polynomial roots in a p-adic closure
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and put $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Let $\Omega/k$ be any algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. The base $k$ is complete, nontrivially normed, nonarchimedean and of characteristic zero, and $\mathbf Q$ is dense in $k$: for $z\in k$ and $r>0$ some $q\in\mathbf Q$ satisfies $|z-q|_\ell<r$. There is a real-valued norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\Omega$ extending $|\cdot|_\ell$, satisfying $\|z\|\geq0$, $\|z\|=0\Leftrightarrow z=0$, $\|1\|=1$, $\|zw\|=\|z\|\|w\|$ and $\|z+w\|\leq\max\{\|z\|,\|w\|\}$, and giving distance $d(z,w)=\|z-w\|$. For every $x\in\Omega$, its minimal polynomial $f\in k[T]$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension, def-weil-polynomial-ring] is monic, irreducible and separable [def-pc-separable-polynomial], has degree $n\geq1$, satisfies $f(x)=0$ [def-weil-polynomial-root], and splits into $n$ distinct linear factors in $\Omega[T]$. In particular the set $S=\{y\in\Omega:f(y)=0,\ y\ne x\}$ is finite. Define $\delta=1$ if $S=\varnothing$, and otherwise $\delta=\min\{\|x-y\|:y\in S\}$. Then $\delta>0$ and $\delta\leq\|x-y\|$ for every $y\in S$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $k$ is the completion of $\mathbf Q$ for $|\cdot|_\ell$, is complete and nonarchimedean, and has characteristic zero. Its norm is nontrivial since $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$. By the definition of completion, each $z\in k$ is represented by a rational Cauchy sequence $q_j$ converging to $z$. For $r>0$, choose $j$ with $|z-q_j|_\ell<r$. This proves the stated density.

proof.text: The extension $\Omega/k$ is algebraic by [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Apply [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension] with $F=k$, $L=\Omega$: step 1 checks completeness, nontriviality and the nonarchimedean hypothesis. Take its spectral norm as $\|\cdot\|$. Its nonnegative real values, definiteness, unit, product and strong triangle laws give all the requested norm identities, and its stated distance is $d(z,w)=\|z-w\|$.

source.place: spectralNorm_extends, line 573; isNonarchimedean_spectralNorm, line 645; spectralNorm.normedField, lines 854–870.

proof.text: Fix $x\in\Omega$. Algebraicity in [def-weil-algebraic-closure] permits its minimal polynomial $f$ in [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; that statement gives monicity, irreducibility and $f(x)=0$. Write $n=\deg f$. By [def-weil-polynomial-ring], a monic polynomial of degree zero is $1$, which evaluates to $1\ne0$ by [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Hence $n\geq1$.

proof.text: The derivative formula in [def-pc-separable-polynomial] shows that the coefficient of $T^{n-1}$ in $f\prime$ is $n$, since $f$ is monic. This is nonzero in characteristic zero, so $f\prime\ne0$. The irreducibility from step 3 and [lem-trf-irreducible-separable-derivative] imply separability. Now [lem-pc-separable-polynomial-distinct-roots-alg-closed], applied to $F=k$, $P=f$ and the given algebraically closed $\Omega$, supplies exactly $n$ distinct roots and the asserted factorization into linear factors.

source.place: Tag 09H0, lemma-irreducible-polynomials, characteristic-zero argument; distinct-root factorization as in the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The root set in step 4 is finite, so its subset $S$ is finite. For $y\in S$, $x-y\ne0$, hence definiteness and nonnegativity give $\|x-y\|>0$. If $S$ is empty, $\delta=1>0$ and the bound is vacuous. Otherwise its distance image is a finite nonempty set of positive reals: successive binary minima produce a member $a>0$ no larger than any member (start with a singleton and replace $a$ by $\min(a,b)$ when adjoining $b$). Thus its minimum $\delta$ exists, is positive, and satisfies $\delta\leq\|x-y\|$ for every $y\in S$.
